title: Designing Leadership Teams for Architectural and Integrative Work
author: Hart, Nick
source: A Change is Gonna Come, April 11, 2026
summary: Schools typically structure leadership teams around hierarchy and generalist roles, placing heavy burden on individuals to quickly master multiple domains. Hart proposes redesigning teams to distinguish between architectural work (designing systems) and integrative work (applying systems in context). Specialist roles handle architecture within domains; generalist roles handle integration across domains. This structural change reduces dependence on individual brilliance and burnout, making leadership sustainable.
points: Most schools' leadership structures are hierarchical and generalist, causing individuals to master too many unrelated domains at once.
Two distinct types of work are needed: architects who design frameworks and integrators who apply them in context.
Specialist roles reduce the expectation that assistant headteachers master everything; they focus on deep expertise in one domain.
Integrative roles become primarily about applying frameworks coherently across the school, not designing from scratch.
System design matters more than individual capability—good structures work even with ordinary staff working ordinary hours.
quotes: Schools that depend on brilliance or burnout eventually run out of both.
The effectiveness of the system depends on how quickly individuals can compensate for the way the system is designed.
The issue is not that Helen lacks capability. It is that the role asks her to carry too many types of work at once.
Clarity is not left to chance and coherence is not left to individuals. Both become features of the system itself.

The more closely this alignment is achieved, the less leadership depends on individual effort and the more it becomes a property of the system itself.” Archived from A Change is Gonna Come on May 2, 2026 by Tim.
